property_summary: The SetMinSum function does not revert when called before Initialized, so MinSum can be set.
After Collect(uint256) is called, calling SetMinSum with a value does not revert and changes MinSum to that value.
Collect(uint256) never changes MinSum
After Collect is called, MinSum remains equal to the value set by the last successful SetMinSum call.
Collect never reverts if the caller has sufficient balance and the unlock time has passed.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its initial value.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable equals its value before the call.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable equals the value set by the last SetMinSum call.
After any Collect call, the value of MinSum equals the value set by SetMinSum (which is nonzero in the reference, but zero in the mutant).

After any call to Collect, MinSum remains equal to the value it had before that call, which is a property satisfied by the reference where SetMinSum stores the input, but broken by the mutant that sets MinSum to 0.
When Collect is called with any amount, the stored MinSum value must be the original value set, not incremented.
After any public interaction ending with Collect, the public state variable MinSum must equal the value last set via SetMinSum (not incremented by 1).
After any sequence of valid public calls ending with Collect, the MinSum state variable must equal the last value passed to SetMinSum before initialization.
After Collect completes, MinSum equals the last value passed to SetMinSum before initialization.
After any public call sequence ending with Collect, the value of MinSum must equal the value last set by SetMinSum (and not that value plus one).
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable equals its initial value (0) if the contract has not been initialized.
After any Collect call, the value of MinSum remains unchanged, regardless of whether the contract was initialized.
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable remains equal to its initial value (0) when the contract has been initialized.
After any Collect call, the MinSum state variable is unchanged and equals its initial value set before initialization.
After calling SetMinSum with a non-zero value and then Initialized, any subsequent Collect call never changes MinSum from that non-zero value.
After calling Collect, the SetLogFile address is always the original log address if initialization flag is false; but the mutant changes it.
When SetLogFile is not yet initialized (intitalized is false), calling Collect never reverts, regardless of the input parameters.
After calling Collect, the LogFile address in state remains unchanged (equal to the one set during initialization) regardless of the call parameters.
After calling Collect, the SetLogFile address is always the original log address if initialization flag is false; but the mutant changes it.
After calling Collect, the owner of the C contract can always call SetLogFile without reverting if intitalized is false.
The balance of a user remains unchanged after calling Collect when the contract is not initialized.
After Collect is called, the Log state variable equals the address originally set via SetLogFile.
After Collect is called, the Log state variable is set to the address passed to SetLogFile, which should be equal to the address of the deployed LogFile contract.
After Collect is called, the Log state variable is set to the address originally passed to SetLogFile (which is the address of the deployed LogFile contract), not a constant address.
After Collect is called, the address stored in the public Log getter matches the address set via SetLogFile.
After Collect reduces balance by _am, the new balance equals old balance minus _am.
After a successful Collect call, the balance of the caller's account decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After Collect, the contract's total ether balance decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance in the mapping does not increase.
After a Collect call, the caller's reported balance in the Acc mapping is never greater than before the call.
Collect only reduces balance when caller's balance is at least MinSum.
After Collect is called, the caller's balance is never less than MinSum when the call succeeds (Collect does not revert).
Collect only allows withdrawal when the caller's balance is at least MinSum.
If the contract collects from a caller with balance >= MinSum, the caller's balance after collect must be <= old balance minus claimed amount.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance is never reduced when it was below MinSum before the call.
Collecting funds must not be possible before the unlock time has passed.
The contract balance before and after a Collect call must be the same when the caller has less than MinSum balance.
The unlockTime of the caller's holder after a Collect call must remain unchanged if the call reverted or did not execute due to insufficient balance.
After a call to Collect, the caller's balance in the contract must decrease exactly by the amount they requested if the call succeeded and the timestamp is greater than the unlock time.
After a Collect call, the contract's total balance should only decrease when the caller's unlock time has passed.
After Collect, the balance of msg.sender in the contract should not increase (it should decrease by _am or stay the same).
The balance of msg.sender in the contract should decrease by exactly _am when Collect succeeds
When Collect succeeds (calls Log.AddMessage without reverting), the stored balance of the caller must be less than or equal to the balance before Collect.

After Collect reverts or succeeds, the caller's stored balance in the contract must be exactly the value immediately before the Collect call minus the withdrawal amount (or unchanged if the transfer fails).
After a successful Collect (i.e., the call does not revert), the caller's stored balance must be at least MinSum lower than before the call.
Collect should only succeed when the requested amount is at least as large as the balance.
Collect should fail when the requested amount exceeds the balance
After Collect(uint256) reverts, the balance should not decrease.
The balance after Collect is not greater than the maximum of MinSum and the amount requested.
After a successful Collect call, the returned balance is exactly the initial balance minus the amount collected.
